reason: H0 still derives triangle_filter_for_2to1 as a bool and passes it positionally to S1's uint8_t ycc_upsampling parameter, so it supplies only 0 or 1. S1 assigns distinct behavior to nonzero values: 1 selects the libjpeg h2v2 triangle implementation with odd-column rounding 7, while every other nonzero value selects the libwebp implementation with rounding 8. Consequently H0 cannot exercise the new libwebp branch. Its crash-only check also cannot validate the intentionally different rounded pixel output.
evidence: In fuzz_swizzle_ycck, triangle_filter_for_2to1 is declared bool and set from one hash bit: `bool triangle_filter_for_2to1 = 1 & (hash >> 38)`.
That bool is passed as the penultimate semantic argument to wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__swizzle_ycck, whose S1 signature replaces `bool triangle_filter_for_2to1` with `uint8_t ycc_upsampling`.

S1 selects `wuffs_private_impl__swizzle_ycc__upsample_inv_h2v2_triangle_libjpeg` only when `ycc_upsampling == 1`; otherwise any nonzero value selects `wuffs_private_impl__swizzle_ycc__upsample_inv_h2v2_triangle_libwebp`. The same split exists for the `_x86_avx2` functions.
The libjpeg and libwebp wrappers pass different `odd_column_rounding` values, 7 and 8 respectively, into the changed h2v2 triangle implementations.
H0 only calls swizzle_ycck and accepts any non-internal-error status; it makes no assertion about destination pixels or agreement between the libjpeg/libwebp, scalar, and AVX2 paths.
recommended_action: Replace the boolean selector with fuzzed `uint8_t ycc_upsampling` values that deliberately cover 0, 1, and at least one nonzero value other than 1. Add output checks using rounding-sensitive source samples, and where available compare scalar and AVX2 results separately for the libjpeg and libwebp h2v2 triangle branches.
